stories.title: Greenstone Partners Brokers Two Chicago Multifamily Transactions
stories.excerpt: Greenstone Partners closed two multifamily transactions totaling $3.27 million across Chicago’s Wicker Park and Bridgeport neighborhoods. The transactions were facilitated by Greenstone Partners Partner Jordan Multack, with Director Jacob Goldstein also representing the firm on the Bridgeport transaction. The transactions include the sale of 1226 N. Greenview Ave. in Wicker Park for $2.245 million and 3201–3203 S. May St. in Bridgeport for $1.025 million. Multack represented the transaction involving 1226 N. Greenview Ave., a recently renovated, eight-unit multifamily property located in Chicago’s highly desirable Wicker Park neighborhood. The 6,500-square-foot property features one- and two-bedroom units. Multack and Goldstein represented the transaction involving 3201–3203 S. May St. in Chicago’s Bridgeport neighborhood. The property consists of a three-unit multifamily building with an additional non-conforming coach house, together with an adjacent development lot. The property offered a combination of existing rental income and future value-creation opportunities, including potential rent growth, additional parking income, and development optionality through the separately parceled adjacent lot. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. bullets: Greenstone Partners closed $3.27M in Chicago multifamily sales across Wicker Park and Bridgeport.
Wicker Park 8-unit property sold for $2.245M; Bridgeport 3-unit plus development lot for $1.025M.
Bridgeport transaction includes adjacent development parcel and value-creation optionality for future upside.
stories.summary: Greenstone Partners brokered two small multifamily transactions totaling $3.27 million in Chicago's Wicker Park and Bridgeport neighborhoods. The Wicker Park sale ($2.245M) involved a recently renovated 8-unit building; the Bridgeport transaction ($1.025M) included a 3-unit building plus a separately parceled development lot. The Bridgeport deal explicitly signals value-creation potential through rent growth, parking income, and future development optionality.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact. These are small, sub-$3M trades in secondary/tertiary neighborhoods with no scale signal. However, the Bridgeport transaction's structure—existing income + development lot—indicates developers see feasibility and upside in infill redevelopment on the city's South Side. Worth monitoring if similar packaged lots attract institutional capital.

stories.title: Community Roots Housing, Kids Co. Launch Buildout of Learning Center at Seattle Housing Development
stories.excerpt: Community Roots Housing and Kids Co. have begun construction on a new early learning center at CopperLeaf Northgate, one of Seattle’s newest affordable housing communities. The new 7,761-square-foot center and outdoor play area will transform the ground-floor space at CopperLeaf into a purpose-built early learning environment. The project also represents a historic milestone for Kids Co., marking its first standalone early learning center outside a Seattle Public Schools building. Construction is now underway, led by Walsh Construction as general contractor and CAST Architecture for architecture and interior design. Located adjacent to Northgate Station, the child care center builds on the vision behind the apartment building, which opened earlier this year and is now fully leased. As a transit-oriented affordable housing community, CopperLeaf is intentionally designed to connect residents with services and amenities. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. bullets: Community Roots Housing and Kids Co. breaking ground on 7,761 SF early learning center at CopperLeaf Northgate, Seattle.
CopperLeaf affordable housing opened earlier this year, already fully leased adjacent to Northgate Station.
Transit-oriented design with integrated childcare addresses supply-side amenity demand and workforce housing stickiness.
stories.summary: Community Roots Housing and Kids Co. have begun construction on a purpose-built early learning center within CopperLeaf Northgate, a new affordable housing community in Seattle. The 7,761-square-foot center transforms ground-floor space at the TOD property, which opened and fully leased earlier in 2024. The project, led by Walsh Construction and CAST Architecture, represents Kids Co.'s first standalone early learning facility outside a public school building.
stories.impact: Seattle TOD multifamily developers should note strong absorption and immediate full lease-up of CopperLeaf, signaling robust demand for transit-adjacent affordable housing with integrated family services. Integrated childcare reduces tenant turnover and justifies premium positioning—a playbook for Northgate and similar Seattle TOD sites where transit + affordability + services = rapid absorption and strong retention.

stories.title: Simone Development Leases Up Mount Vernon Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Simone Development Companies has signed two new leases totaling 36,000 square feet at its Mount Vernon, NY industrial center, marking the full lease-up of the two-story, 63,445-square-foot property. Located at 560 South Third Avenue, the facility features on-site parking, high clear ceiling heights, and a drive-in and loading dock, along with convenient access to the Hutchinson River Parkway, I-95 North and South, and U.S. Route 1. “The full lease-up of 560 South Third Avenue reinforces Mount Vernon’s essential role in the regional supply chain,” said Joanna Simone, President of Leasing and Property Management Operations for Simone Development in a statement. The family-owned real estate investment firm has a portfolio exceeding 7 million square feet across the New York City area. Elsewhere in Mount Vernon, a joint venture of Simone Development and Stagg Group recently topped off QWest Towers, a $158-million workforce housing development at 1 and 25 North MacQuesten Pkwy. The post Simone Development Leases Up Mount Vernon Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Simone Development achieved full lease-up of 63,445 SF industrial property at 560 South Third Avenue, Mount Vernon, NY.
Separately, Simone/Stagg JV topped off QWest Towers, a $158M workforce housing development at 1 and 25 North MacQuesten Pkwy.
Mount Vernon fills regional supply-chain role; QWest Towers signals workforce housing pipeline in lower Westchester market.
stories.summary: Simone Development Companies fully leased a 63,445-square-foot, two-story industrial facility in Mount Vernon, NY, marking completion of lease-up at 560 South Third Avenue. Separately, a Simone/Stagg Group joint venture topped off QWest Towers, a $158 million workforce housing development at North MacQuesten Parkway in Mount Vernon. The industrial lease-up reflects Mount Vernon's regional supply-chain role; the JV housing development signals workforce housing absorption in lower Westchester.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily signal in Article 3 itself, but the QWest Towers mention is worth monitoring: a $158M workforce housing project in Mount Vernon suggests demand and capital activity in lower Westchester's commuter-shed markets near NYC. If QWest leases quickly and PRN commute patterns hold post-COVID, the Westchester-to-NYC corridor becomes attractive for multifamily development ahead of broader regional in-migration.

stories.title: CedarSt Lands $80M for San Diego Multifamily Project
stories.excerpt: CedarSt Companies has secured $80 million in construction financing for a 197-unit apartment development in San Diego’s North Park neighborhood. CrossHarbor Capital Partners provided the three-year, floating-rate stretch-senior loan for the Samuel, an eight-story Class A project planned for 2821 Adams Avenue. JLL Capital Markets announced the loan Monday, and JLL’s Zach Kersten, Jack Wood and Ben Choromanski arranged the financing for CedarSt. Construction is scheduled to begin in the third quarter, with completion expected in late 2028. The Samuel will include 82 studios, 93 one-bedroom units and 22 two-bedroom units, averaging 621 square feet, along with 189 parking spaces. The project qualifies for ministerial by-right approvals through San Diego’s Complete Communities program, which expedites residential projects near transit and existing infrastructure. “North Park continues to attract young professionals seeking walkable urban living at a relative value compared to coastal neighborhoods,” Kersten said in a statement, adding that few large-scale multifamily projects have been built or planned within a mile of the site. North Park maintains an average multifamily occupancy rate of 96 percent, according to JLL, which projects average annual rent growth of 3.52 percent in the submarket through 2029. The Samuel is part of a larger San Diego expansion for Chicago-based CedarSt. The developer has assembled a six-project pipeline totaling 1,514 units and $734 million in development costs across the region. Nationally, CedarSt manages more than 7,000 units across 35 properties valued at an estimated $4 billion. Meanwhile, CrossHarbor manages $11 billion in assets and has completed more than $34 billion in investments since its founding in 1993. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CedarSt secured $80M construction financing from CrossHarbor Capital for 197-unit apartment in San Diego's North Park.
Samuel project: 8-story Class A, 82 studios/93 1BR/22 2BR, ministerial approval via Complete Communities program, Q3 2024 start, late 2028 delivery.
North Park positioning young professionals seeking walkable urban living at relative value vs. coastal neighborhoods; project qualifies for by-right approvals.
stories.summary: CedarSt Companies secured $80 million in three-year floating-rate construction financing from CrossHarbor Capital Partners for The Samuel, a 197-unit, eight-story apartment project in San Diego's North Park neighborhood at 2821 Adams Avenue. The Class A development—comprising 82 studios, 93 one-bedroom, and 22 two-bedroom units averaging 621 sf—qualifies for ministerial by-right approval under San Diego's Complete Communities program. Construction is slated to begin Q3 2024 with delivery in late 2028.
stories.impact: San Diego North Park continues to signal strong multifamily demand and favorable regulatory environment. By-right approvals via Complete Communities program accelerate entitlements and de-risk financing for transit-proximate projects. The studio/1BR bias (89% of units) and modest $621 sf average target young professionals arbitraging North Park's walkability against coastal premium—a repeatable playbook suggesting underutilized TOD upside in mid-tier San Diego submarkets before coastal saturation.

stories.title: Terra Nabs $245M Permanent Loan for 47-acre Project in Miami-Dade
stories.excerpt: Terra has secured a $245 million permanent loan for the first phase of a 47-acre transit-oriented development near the edge of Miami-Dade County, the Miami-based development firm announced. The financing from Slate Property Group covers 578 apartments within the Upland Park mixed-use development at 1455 Northwest 121st Avenue, part of county-owned land adjacent to Dolphin Station Park and Ride Transit Terminal. The first phase — completed this year — includes nine garden-style residential buildings, each three stories tall. They’re located west of the Dolphin Mall, near the intersection between the Florida Turnpike and Dolphin Expressway. New York-based Slate Property Group had provided the $170 million construction loan in 2024. Today, more than 60 percent of apartments have been leased, with monthly rents starting at $2,000, according to a representative for Terra, which is led by David Martin. Later this year, the developer expects to break ground on the second phase, which will feature 484 apartments. In 2021, Terra struck a 97-year ground lease with Miami-Dade County, which projected earning nearly $1.2 billion during the lease term. In all, Upland Park is expected to house more apartments as well as retail and commercial space, with master-plan architect Arquitectonica and urban planners Plusurbia Design. A representative for the developer declined to provide additional details. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terra secured $245M permanent loan from Slate Property Group for 578-unit Phase 1 of 47-acre mixed-use Upland Park, Miami-Dade.
Phase 1 completed 2024 with 60% leased, rents $2M+/mo; Phase 2 (484 units) breaking ground mid-2024. 97-year ground lease with Miami-Dade County.
Transit-oriented development near Dolphin Station Park & Ride; Slate provided $170M construction loan in 2024, now transitioning to permanent.
stories.summary: Terra secured a $245 million permanent loan from Slate Property Group to cover 578 apartments in Phase 1 of Upland Park, a 47-acre mixed-use TOD in Miami-Dade County near Dolphin Station Park & Ride Transit Terminal. Phase 1, completed in 2024, includes nine 3-story garden-style residential buildings with over 60% leased at rents starting $2,000/month. Terra expects to break ground on Phase 2 (484 units) later in 2024 under a 97-year ground lease with Miami-Dade County.
stories.impact: Miami-Dade multifamily developers should track Upland Park as a proof-of-concept for transit-oriented, county-ground-lease development at scale. Strong absorption (60%+ leased post-delivery) and rapid Phase 2 authorization signal robust demand for workforce/middle-market housing near transit infrastructure in western Miami-Dade. The permanent financing at $245M for Phase 1 (c. $424k/unit) suggests healthy cap rates and investor appetite for TOD multifamily outside dense core—template for future ground-lease projects in underserved transit corridors.

stories.title: CBRE Brokers Sale of Vintage Redlands Apartments
stories.excerpt: CBRE announced the closing of The Kimberly Apartments, a 54-unit multifamily investment at 475 E Cypress Avenue in Redlands, California. Sirott Investments is listed as the owner. Eric Chen and Blake Torgerson exclusively represented the buyer in this transaction. The property traded for $12,.3 million, reflecting $228,704 per unit and $144 per square foot, at a 5.71% current Cap Rate with a compelling 7.84% pro forma Cap Rate, representing significant upside for the new ownership. Built in 1964, the 86,040 SF building sits on over 2.5 acres and features six 1-bedroom/1-bathroom units, forty-two 2-bedroom/2-bathroom units, and six 3-bedroom/2-bathroom units, with spacious house-like units averaging nearly 1,500 square feet. Fully amenitized with a pool, fitness center, laundry facilities, spa, and ample parking, the community is ideally situated across from Albertsons Market, Chase Bank, and Panera Bread, with minutes to charming Downtown Redlands and walking distance to Redlands High School. The post CBRE Brokers Sale of Vintage Redlands Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE closed sale of The Kimberly Apartments, 54-unit vintage property in Redlands, CA, for $12.3M ($228.7k/unit).
1964-built, 86,040 SF on 2.5 acres; current cap rate 5.71%, pro forma cap rate 7.84% reflecting significant upside potential.
Strong amenity suite and retail adjacency (Albertsons, Chase, Panera) near Downtown Redlands; new ownership positioned for value-add.
stories.summary: CBRE facilitated the sale of The Kimberly Apartments, a 54-unit apartment community in Redlands, California, for $12.3 million ($228,704 per unit). Built in 1964, the 86,040-square-foot property on 2.5 acres trades at a current 5.71% cap rate with a 7.84% pro forma cap rate, indicating substantial value-add opportunity for new owner Sirott Investments. The community features spacious units (avg. 1,500 sf), full amenities, and strong retail adjacency near Downtown Redlands.
stories.impact: Limited strategic impact for forward-looking developers. The 7.84% pro forma cap rate reflects older vintage product positioned for near-term rent growth and minor renovations in an Inland Empire submarket. However, the wide gap between current (5.71%) and pro forma (7.84%) cap rates signals cap rate compression in Southern California, constraining new development underwriting and favoring opportunistic value-add acquisitions of legacy stock over ground-up development.

stories.title: El Segundo Rivian R&D Facility Acquired for $27.25M
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the $27.25 million sale of 401 Coral Circle, a 56,815-square-foot R&D office facility located in El Segundo, California. The property is 100% leased on a triple-net (NNN) basis to Rivian. The buyer was Majestic Realty. Newmark’s Kevin Shannon, Rob Hannan, Ken White, Laura Stumm, Michael Moll, Ryan Plummer, Andrew Briner and Aaron Banks represented the seller, Hackman Capital Partners. Hackman Capital Partners originally acquired 401 Coral Circle in 2018 for $15.3 million, repositioned the asset and leased it to Boeing and subsequently Rivian. The $27.25 million sale price, approximately $480 per square foot, represents a 78% increase in value over Hackman’s eight-year hold period and is a testament to the strength and desirability of the South Bay market. Originally built in 1967 and renovated in 2020, the facility serves as both a customer-facing service center and a highly secure R&D facility, supporting Rivian’s consumer and commercial vehicle lines. bullets: Majestic Realty acquired 401 Coral Circle, 56,815 SF R&D facility in El Segundo, from Hackman Capital Partners for $27.25M.
Property 100% NNN-leased to Rivian; Hackman held for 8 years, achieving 78% appreciation ($15.3M to $27.25M purchase price).
Facility renovated 2020, serves as Rivian customer-facing service center and secure R&D for consumer/commercial vehicles.
stories.summary: Newmark brokered the $27.25 million sale of 401 Coral Circle, a 56,815-square-foot R&D office facility in El Segundo, to Majestic Realty from Hackman Capital Partners. The property is 100% leased on an NNN basis to Rivian and serves as both a customer-facing service center and secure R&D facility for Rivian's vehicle lines. Hackman's 8-year hold generated 78% appreciation, with the sale price of $480/sf reflecting strong South Bay market desirability.
stories.impact: Not directly multifamily-relevant, but signals robust demand for industrial/R&D space in South Bay Los Angeles tied to EV and advanced manufacturing. Rivian's need for secure, customer-facing R&D facilities and willingness to pay premium lease rates suggests sustained employer growth and operational footprint in LA metro. If Rivian expands further in South Bay or adjacent markets, job in-migration will drive regional multifamily demand and rent growth in proximity to manufacturing/R&D clusters.

stories.title: Manga Hotels Pays $50M for Second NYC Hotel Acquisition
stories.excerpt: The Chelsean New York Hotel has traded hands for $50 million. The Lam Generation, led by Jeffrey Lam, offloaded the 158-key hotel at 158-162 West 25th Street to Manga Hotel Group in what is the second transaction between the two in a little over a year, according to a deed transfer in property records made public Monday. While the Canada-based buyer is a hotel operator, the 21-story building could be repositioned into a number of uses. Manga focuses on not only hospitality but also residential real estate. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. Manga and Lam did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In February 2025, Manga acquired the 160-key hotel at 54 Watts Street, also known as the SoHo 54 Hotel, which appears to still be in operation, for $56 million. The purchase was Manga’s first foray into the New York City market and the 19-story lodging would be branded under the Toor Hotel Collection. The Chelsean was constructed in 2001, when Eric Brown acquired it as a development site for just $1.6 million in 1999, with Bob Knakal brokering the deal, according to an announcement reposted to the website of his new firm, Bob Knakal Real Estate Advisors. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Manga Hotels acquired The Chelsean (158-key hotel) at 158-162 West 25th Street, Manhattan, for $50M from The Lam Generation.
Second Manga NYC acquisition in 13 months; prior deal (54 Watts Street, SoHo) in Feb 2025 for $56M. Building could be repositioned into residential.
Manga focuses on hospitality and residential real estate; Chelsea location and 21-story building present conversion/hybrid-use optionality.
stories.summary: Manga Hotel Group acquired The Chelsean, a 158-key hotel at 158-162 West 25th Street in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood, for $50 million from The Lam Generation. This marks Manga's second NYC hotel acquisition in roughly 13 months, following a $56 million purchase of the SoHo 54 Hotel (160 keys) in February 2025. The Canada-based buyer operates hotels and invests in residential real estate, suggesting the Chelsea asset could be repositioned into alternative uses.
stories.impact: Not directly multifamily development, but Manga's aggressive NYC hotel acquisition strategy (two deals in 13 months for $106M) and stated focus on residential repositioning signal investor appetite for hotel-to-residential conversions in Manhattan. If occupancy and cap rates on legacy hotels remain compressed, look for increased conversion activity in Manhattan submarkets like Chelsea and SoHo, competing for multifamily development capital and adding supply pressure on new Class A construction in those neighborhoods.

stories.title: Financial Services Firm Aegon Takes 21K SF at 125 West 57th Street
stories.excerpt: International financial services firm Aegon is moving its office kingdom to New York City. Aegon, which was founded in the Netherlands and specializes in life insurance, pensions and retirement plans, has decided on 125 West 57th Street for its new headquarters, inking a 20,600-square-foot lease at the property in Manhattan’s Plaza District owned by Alchemy-ABR Investment Partners and Cain International. The company will occupy two floors in the recently completed, 30-story office building, according to the landlords. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed, but the average asking rent for Class A office space in the Plaza District was $97.23 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to research from Colliers. JLL’s Mitchell Konsker, Kristen Morgan, Christine Colley, Kate Roush and Dan Turkewitz represented ownership in this deal, while Aegon was represented by Barry Zeller and David Downey from Cushman & Wakefield. “125 West 57th’s leasing momentum shows how much tenants value new construction — something the Manhattan market has very little of,” Morgan told Commercial Observer. “Aegon’s decision to relocate is further proof of how well this building is performing in the current market.” C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal comes as part of Aegon’s plans to move its head office and legal operations from the Netherlands to the U.S. and to rename the company Transamerica upon completion of the transaction, which is set to be finished by Jan. 1, 2028, according to ownership. bullets: International financial services firm Aegon signed 20,600 SF lease at 125 West 57th Street (Plaza District, Manhattan) for NYC headquarters.
Two-floor occupancy in recently completed 30-story Class A office building; Class A asking rent Plaza District Q2 2024 = $97.23/SF.
Aegon relocating office HQ to NYC; institutional office leasing activity and HQ consolidation signal stable Manhattan demand, but office-specific, not multifamily.
stories.summary: Aegon, a Netherlands-founded international financial services firm specializing in life insurance, pensions, and retirement plans, signed a 20,600-square-foot lease for two floors at 125 West 57th Street in Manhattan's Plaza District. The lease marks Aegon's establishment of a new U.S. headquarters in the recently completed, 30-story Class A office building. Class A asking rent in the Plaza District averaged $97.23/sf in Q2 2024.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance. Aegon's HQ consolidation to NYC is a positive office-market signal but does not directly drive residential demand. However, large financial services HQ moves to Manhattan can indirectly support multifamily demand through higher-wage job concentration and talent attraction—but only if Aegon expands headcount materially, which is not mentioned.

stories.title: Citadel Credit Union Provides $50M Refi on Philly Office Tower
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between CSB Holdings and Tide Realty Capital has sealed a $50 million loan to refinance a newly acquired Philadelphia office tower, Commercial Observer has learned. Citadel Credit Union supplied the loan on the 29-story office building at 2000 Market Street in Philadelphia’s Center City neighborhood. CSB and Tide Realty teamed up to purchase the asset for $45.5 million last year at a 64 percent discount from Nahla Capital as part of a value-add strategy. The refi will pay off a previous acquisition loan from Maxim Capital and fund a $14 million credit reserve for future leasing. Two50 Capital arranged the transaction with a team led by Adrian Edery. The 668,335-square-foot property was 68 percent occupied at time of the acquisition with existing tenants having a weighted average lease term of 5.5 years, the Philadelphia Business Journal reported at the time. Nahla Capital had partnered with a division of Goldman Sachs to buy the building for $125.4 million in 2018. Edery, principal at Two50 Capital, said the new ownership has boosted leasing occupancy at the 1973-builder property to around 77 percent after inking some major renewals over the past year. Anchor tenants include law firm Marshall Dennehey and Board of Pensions of the Presbyterian Church. “Given how sensitive the office debt markets are in terms of lender appetite, we are deliberate about which operators we are looking to represent as well as the assets we are arranging the debt on,” Edery said in prepared remarks. “We are looking to place debt on Class A and B buildings in the top markets that have genuine positive absorption with the right story.” Citadel Credit Union, CSB Holdings and Tide Realty Capital did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com
bullets: CSB Holdings and Tide Realty Capital refinanced 2000 Market Street, Philadelphia, 29-story, 668k SF office tower with $50M loan from Citadel Credit Union.
JV acquired asset for $45.5M (64% discount from prior 2018 $125.4M purchase by Nahla/Goldman Sachs); building 68% occupied at acquisition.
Value-add repositioning strategy; $14M credit reserve carved out for future leasing; 5.5-year weighted average lease term among existing tenants.
stories.summary: A joint venture between CSB Holdings and Tide Realty Capital secured a $50 million refinance from Citadel Credit Union on 2000 Market Street, a 29-story, 668,335-square-foot office tower in Philadelphia's Center City. The JV acquired the asset last year for $45.5 million—a 64% discount from Nahla Capital's 2018 $125.4 million purchase (done with Goldman Sachs)—and is pursuing a value-add strategy. At acquisition, the property was 68% occupied with a 5.5-year weighted average lease term; the refi funds a $14 million credit reserve for future leasing.
stories.impact: Not multifamily-relevant. Philadelphia office distress and value-add repositioning reflect broader office-market dysfunction and capital redeployment; however, large office towers in Center City are not competing with multifamily for land or capital. Monitor only if conversion-to-residential becomes attractive—unlikely at current market conditions without forced supply removal.
